questions.prompt: In hay conservation, what does forage mainly refer to?
options: Edible pasture plants used as animal feed
Soil removed from a farm path
Water kept in an uncovered bucket
Ash from a cooking fire
questions.correctAnswer: Edible pasture plants used as animal feed
questions.explanation: Forage is plant material such as grasses and legumes that livestock can eat.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify forage materials used for conserving animal feed during dry periods.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of making hay for livestock?
options: To store animal feed for seasons when fresh pasture is scarce
To make drinking water for animals salty
To replace all farm records
To stop animals from eating roughage
questions.correctAnswer: To store animal feed for seasons when fresh pasture is scarce
questions.explanation: Hay provides conserved feed that can be used when pasture is limited, especially during drought.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why forage is conserved as hay to cope with drought.

questions.prompt: Which material is most suitable for making hay?
options: Nutritious grass cut at the right stage
Polythene bags from a market
Wet soil from a drainage channel
Rusty metal pieces from a store
questions.correctAnswer: Nutritious grass cut at the right stage
questions.explanation: Good hay is made from suitable forage plants such as grasses and legumes, not waste materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate plant materials for hay making.

questions.prompt: Why should cut forage be dried before storage as hay?
options: Drying reduces mould and spoilage
Drying turns it into fertilizer immediately
Drying makes it poisonous to pests
Drying removes all nutrients from the feed
questions.correctAnswer: Drying reduces mould and spoilage
questions.explanation: Excess moisture encourages mould, heating, and rotting, so hay should be dried properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe drying as an important step in conserving forage.

questions.prompt: Which sign best shows that hay may be poorly dried and unsafe for storage?
options: A mouldy smell and damp patches
A clean dry texture
A greenish colour with no dampness
A labelled storage date
questions.correctAnswer: A mouldy smell and damp patches
questions.explanation: Mouldy smell and dampness show that hay can spoil and may harm livestock.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize signs of poor-quality conserved forage.

questions.prompt: Which method conserves forage by tying dried material into compact packages?
options: Baling
Flooding
Pruning
Transplanting
questions.correctAnswer: Baling
questions.explanation: Baling compresses dried forage into packages that are easier to handle, store, and transport.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify baling as a method of conserving forage.

questions.prompt: What is standing forage in animal feed conservation?
options: Forage left growing in the field for later grazing or harvesting
Feed mixed with dirty water before storage
Hay stored directly on a wet floor
Vegetables cooked before planting
questions.correctAnswer: Forage left growing in the field for later grazing or harvesting
questions.explanation: Standing forage keeps feed available in the field so animals can use it later when fresh feed is scarce.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe standing forage as a way of conserving animal feed.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps protect stored hay from moisture?
options: Keeping it under a roof on a raised dry platform
Leaving it uncovered during rain
Sprinkling water on it daily
Pressing it into a drainage ditch
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping it under a roof on a raised dry platform
questions.explanation: A raised dry platform and roof reduce moisture, which helps prevent mould and nutrient loss.
questions.learningOutcome: State safe storage practices for conserved forage.

questions.prompt: Which forage conservation method is usually possible with simple local materials when a baler is unavailable?
options: Stacking dried forage carefully
Using a tractor to deep plough
Mixing feed with kerosene
Burning crop residues in the field
questions.correctAnswer: Stacking dried forage carefully
questions.explanation: Stacking can conserve dry forage or crop residues using locally available supports and covers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify low-cost methods of conserving forage with local resources.

questions.prompt: Which crop residue can be stacked as roughage for livestock after harvesting?
options: Maize stover
Broken glass
Used batteries
Paint tins
questions.correctAnswer: Maize stover
questions.explanation: Maize stover is a plant residue that can be dried and stored as roughage for some livestock.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize crop residues that may be conserved as animal feed.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to make hay during cloudy weather. Which decision is safest?
options: Wait for enough dry weather before final storage
Store the wet forage immediately
Mix damp forage with soil
Cover fresh forage with plastic before drying
questions.correctAnswer: Wait for enough dry weather before final storage
questions.explanation: Hay needs proper drying before storage; storing damp forage encourages mould and heating.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply weather considerations when planning hay making.

questions.prompt: Why are legumes useful in hay mixtures?
options: They can improve the protein value of the feed
They make hay waterproof without drying
They remove the need for clean storage
They make all weeds safe to feed
questions.correctAnswer: They can improve the protein value of the feed
questions.explanation: Legumes are often more protein-rich than many grasses, so they can improve feed quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how forage choice affects the quality of conserved feed.

questions.prompt: A school keeps hay directly on a cement floor that sometimes gets wet. What is the best improvement?
options: Place the hay on pallets and keep the room dry
Spray the floor with more water
Remove all ventilation from the store
Store the hay outside without a cover
questions.correctAnswer: Place the hay on pallets and keep the room dry
questions.explanation: Pallets reduce contact with floor moisture, and a dry store helps hay keep its quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve storage conditions for conserved animal feed.

questions.prompt: Which record would best help a farmer manage stored hay?
options: Date stored, quantity, source, and condition during checks
Names of visitors only
Colour of the store door only
Number of plates in the kitchen
questions.correctAnswer: Date stored, quantity, source, and condition during checks
questions.explanation: Useful feed records help the farmer monitor stock, quality, and storage problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Keep simple records for conserved animal feed.

questions.prompt: What is one advantage of baled hay compared with loose hay?
options: It is easier to stack and transport
It never needs dry storage
It cannot be eaten by livestock
It grows again after harvesting
questions.correctAnswer: It is easier to stack and transport
questions.explanation: Bales are compact, so they are usually easier to carry, count, stack, and store.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare handling qualities of different hay conservation methods.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows basic hay making?
options: Cut suitable forage, dry it, turn it, then store it safely
Store wet forage, cut it later, then dry the store
Burn forage, soak ash, then feed it to animals
Plant maize, harvest cobs, then ignore residues
questions.correctAnswer: Cut suitable forage, dry it, turn it, then store it safely
questions.explanation: Hay making requires harvesting good forage, drying it well, and storing it safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange the main steps in hay making in the correct order.

questions.prompt: A farmer has little money, plenty of dry maize stover, and a dry shed. Which feed conservation choice is most practical?
options: Stack the stover neatly in the dry shed
Buy expensive machinery before saving any feed
Throw the stover into a swamp
Leave all crop residues to rot in the rain
questions.correctAnswer: Stack the stover neatly in the dry shed
questions.explanation: The farmer can use available dry crop residue and storage to conserve roughage at low cost.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable forage conservation methods based on available resources.

questions.prompt: Why should a farmer compare storage space, labour, weather, and forage type before choosing a hay method?
options: These factors affect cost, quality, and success of conservation
They make all hay methods exactly the same
They only matter after animals get sick
They replace the need to dry forage
questions.correctAnswer: These factors affect cost, quality, and success of conservation
questions.explanation: A suitable method depends on local conditions, available labour, storage, and the forage being conserved.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze factors that influence the choice of forage conservation methods.

questions.prompt: Why is conserving leftover food useful in a household?
options: It reduces waste and can provide safe food for later use
It makes food dirty so that pests avoid it
It removes the need to cook hygienically
It turns spoiled food into fresh food
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces waste and can provide safe food for later use
questions.explanation: Safe conservation of leftovers helps reduce food loss and supports household food security.
questions.learningOutcome: State the importance of conserving leftover food safely.

questions.prompt: Which leftover food should be discarded instead of conserved for later eating?
options: Food with a bad smell and visible mould
Clean cooked food cooled quickly
Food stored in a covered clean container
Dry grains kept away from pests
questions.correctAnswer: Food with a bad smell and visible mould
questions.explanation: Bad smell and mould are signs of spoilage; unsafe leftovers should not be eaten.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify unsafe leftover food that should not be reused.

questions.prompt: What is the safest first step before handling leftover food?
options: Wash hands and use clean utensils
Taste every leftover with unwashed fingers
Place food on the floor
Mix all leftovers with raw waste
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands and use clean utensils
questions.explanation: Clean hands and utensils reduce contamination when handling food for storage or reuse.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe hygiene when conserving leftover foods.

questions.prompt: Which container is best for storing safe leftover food?
options: A clean covered container
A rusty open tin
A dirty sack
A broken pesticide bottle
questions.correctAnswer: A clean covered container
questions.explanation: Clean covered containers protect leftovers from dust, insects, and other contaminants.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable containers for conserving leftover foods.

questions.prompt: Why should cooked leftovers be cooled and covered before storage?
options: To reduce contamination and slow spoilage
To attract more flies
To make the food raw again
To increase moisture on the floor
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce contamination and slow spoilage
questions.explanation: Cooling and covering food properly helps keep it safer for later use.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe handling steps for conserving cooked leftover foods.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to reuse leftover rice the next day. Which action is most responsible?
options: Store it covered in a cool clean place and reheat it thoroughly
Leave it uncovered near a dustbin overnight
Mix it with raw meat juice
Keep it in direct sun for two days
questions.correctAnswer: Store it covered in a cool clean place and reheat it thoroughly
questions.explanation: Safe storage and thorough reheating reduce the risk of food-borne illness.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe storage and reheating practices for leftover foods.

questions.prompt: Which leftover is most suitable for composting rather than eating?
options: Vegetable peelings from clean preparation
Fresh chapati kept covered
Clean boiled beans cooled safely
Milk stored in a refrigerator
questions.correctAnswer: Vegetable peelings from clean preparation
questions.explanation: Vegetable peelings are organic waste that can improve compost instead of being eaten as leftovers.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate uses for different leftover food materials.

questions.prompt: Which practice best reduces leftover food waste during a class cooking activity?
options: Plan portions before cooking and store safe leftovers properly
Cook without measuring any ingredients
Throw away all safe food after serving
Mix spoiled food with fresh food
questions.correctAnswer: Plan portions before cooking and store safe leftovers properly
questions.explanation: Planning amounts and storing safe leftovers reduce waste and protect food safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan food preparation to reduce wastage and conserve safe leftovers.

questions.prompt: A family has leftover vegetables and ugali that are still safe. Which plan best conserves them for supper?
options: Keep them separately in clean covered containers and reheat well
Pile them uncovered beside the sink
Mix them with kitchen sweepings
Store them in a container that held pesticide
questions.correctAnswer: Keep them separately in clean covered containers and reheat well
questions.explanation: Separate clean storage and thorough reheating maintain safety and quality for later eating.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe leftover conservation practices in household situations.

questions.prompt: Why is it risky to keep leftovers uncovered in a warm kitchen overnight?
options: Microorganisms and pests can contaminate the food
The food automatically becomes more nutritious
The food becomes dry hay for cattle
The container becomes easier to wash
questions.correctAnswer: Microorganisms and pests can contaminate the food
questions.explanation: Warm uncovered food can spoil quickly and attract flies, rodents, or other contaminants.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze food safety risks when conserving leftover foods.

questions.prompt: What is integrated farming?
options: Combining crops, livestock, and other farm enterprises so resources support each other
Growing only one crop every season
Keeping all farm waste unused
Buying food without producing anything
questions.correctAnswer: Combining crops, livestock, and other farm enterprises so resources support each other
questions.explanation: Integrated farming links enterprises so outputs from one activity can support another.
questions.learningOutcome: Define integrated farming as a resource-conserving production system.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows integrated farming?
options: Using poultry manure to fertilize a vegetable garden
Burning all manure behind the store
Leaving crop residues in a drain
Keeping livestock away from all farm planning
questions.correctAnswer: Using poultry manure to fertilize a vegetable garden
questions.explanation: This links livestock and crop production by using manure as a useful input.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of resource flow in integrated farming.

questions.prompt: Which farm component can provide manure for crop production?
options: Livestock unit
Empty blackboard
Broken radio
Concrete wall
questions.correctAnswer: Livestock unit
questions.explanation: Livestock such as poultry, rabbits, cattle, or goats can provide manure for crops when handled safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify farm components that supply useful resources in an integrated system.

questions.prompt: Why does integrated farming help conserve resources?
options: It reuses materials such as manure, crop residues, and water more efficiently
It makes every farm enterprise isolated
It requires farmers to waste all by-products
It prevents planning between crop and animal units
questions.correctAnswer: It reuses materials such as manure, crop residues, and water more efficiently
questions.explanation: Resource reuse reduces waste, lowers costs, and improves farm sustainability.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how integrated farming conserves farm resources.

questions.prompt: Which output from a maize plot can support livestock in an integrated farm?
options: Maize stover used as roughage
Plastic wrappers used as feed
Broken glass used as bedding
Dirty engine oil used as medicine
questions.correctAnswer: Maize stover used as roughage
questions.explanation: Crop residues such as maize stover can be conserved and used as roughage for some animals.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how crop by-products can support animal production.

questions.prompt: A school keeps rabbits and grows vegetables. Which link would make the system more integrated?
options: Compost rabbit manure safely for the vegetable beds
Throw manure into the classroom
Feed rabbits with plastic waste
Stop recording crop growth
questions.correctAnswer: Compost rabbit manure safely for the vegetable beds
questions.explanation: Composted manure can improve soil fertility and links animal keeping with crop production.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrated farming links in a school agriculture project.

questions.prompt: Which record would best help learners evaluate an integrated farming project?
options: Inputs, outputs, reused wastes, costs, and observed benefits
Only the colour of animal houses
Names of learners without farm data
A list of unrelated songs
questions.correctAnswer: Inputs, outputs, reused wastes, costs, and observed benefits
questions.explanation: Integrated farming records should show how resources move and whether the project saves costs or reduces waste.
questions.learningOutcome: Use records to monitor resource use in integrated farming.

questions.prompt: A farm has a fish pond, vegetable beds, and poultry. Which resource flow is most suitable?
options: Use composted poultry manure to improve vegetable beds under guidance
Pour detergent into the fish pond
Feed birds with spoilt mouldy food
Drain pond water into a dirty pit only
questions.correctAnswer: Use composted poultry manure to improve vegetable beds under guidance
questions.explanation: Safe manure use supports crop growth and connects farm enterprises responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe resource flows among components of an integrated farm.

questions.prompt: Which risk must be managed when using manure in an integrated farm?
options: Disease contamination if manure is handled or applied carelessly
Crops becoming unable to use nutrients
Soil instantly turning into plastic
Water no longer being needed by plants
questions.correctAnswer: Disease contamination if manure is handled or applied carelessly
questions.explanation: Manure is useful but must be composted, handled hygienically, and applied safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safety considerations in integrated farming systems.

questions.prompt: Which plan best shows creativity in designing a small integrated school farm?
options: Link vegetables, rabbits, compost, water saving, records, and safe waste handling
Plant one crop and discard every by-product
Keep animals without feed, water, or records
Use only purchased fertilizer and burn all residues
questions.correctAnswer: Link vegetables, rabbits, compost, water saving, records, and safe waste handling
questions.explanation: A strong integrated plan connects enterprises, conserves resources, and includes safety and records.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple integrated farming plan for a school or home project.

questions.prompt: What is organic gardening mainly based on?
options: Using natural methods to improve soil and manage crops
Using only synthetic chemicals for every problem
Growing crops without soil or water
Avoiding all crop care after planting
questions.correctAnswer: Using natural methods to improve soil and manage crops
questions.explanation: Organic gardening emphasizes compost, mulching, crop rotation, and other natural soil and pest management practices.
questions.learningOutcome: Define organic gardening as a natural approach to crop production.

questions.prompt: Which input is commonly used to improve soil in organic gardening?
options: Well-prepared compost
Leaking battery acid
Plastic pellets
Used paint thinner
questions.correctAnswer: Well-prepared compost
questions.explanation: Compost adds organic matter and nutrients that improve soil structure and fertility.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify organic inputs used to improve soil fertility.

questions.prompt: Why is mulch useful in an organic vegetable garden?
options: It conserves soil moisture and reduces weed growth
It blocks all air from reaching plants
It makes soil sterile forever
It replaces sunlight for leaves
questions.correctAnswer: It conserves soil moisture and reduces weed growth
questions.explanation: Mulch covers the soil, slows evaporation, suppresses weeds, and can add organic matter as it decomposes.
questions.learningOutcome: State the benefits of mulching in organic gardening.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps break pest and disease cycles in an organic garden?
options: Crop rotation
Planting the same crop in the same bed every season
Leaving diseased plants in the bed
Watering only the footpath
questions.correctAnswer: Crop rotation
questions.explanation: Changing crop families in a bed over seasons can reduce buildup of specific pests and diseases.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how crop rotation supports organic pest and disease management.

questions.prompt: Which pair best fits an organic gardening approach?
options: Compost and hand weeding
Pesticide overuse and bare soil
Burning mulch and wasting water
Dumping plastics and skipping records
questions.correctAnswer: Compost and hand weeding
questions.explanation: Compost and hand weeding are practical organic methods for soil fertility and weed control.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable practices for organic crop production.

questions.prompt: A school organic garden has dry soil and many weeds. Which action should learners try first?
options: Apply organic mulch around the crops
Remove all crops and pour oil on the soil
Leave weeds to cover the crop leaves
Stop watering permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Apply organic mulch around the crops
questions.explanation: Mulch helps conserve water, suppress weeds, and protect the soil surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply organic gardening practices to solve moisture and weed problems.

questions.prompt: Which material should not be placed in a school compost heap?
options: Plastic bottle tops
Vegetable peelings
Dry leaves
Grass clippings
questions.correctAnswer: Plastic bottle tops
questions.explanation: Plastic does not decompose into useful compost and should be separated from organic materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Sort materials suitable for composting in organic gardening.

questions.prompt: Which observation best shows that compost is ready for use?
options: It is dark, crumbly, and has an earthy smell
It contains fresh plastic wrappers
It smells strongly of rotting food
It is full of sharp metal pieces
questions.correctAnswer: It is dark, crumbly, and has an earthy smell
questions.explanation: Mature compost is usually dark and crumbly, with no strong unpleasant smell.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize mature compost for use in crop production.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports beneficial insects in an organic garden?
options: Planting flowering herbs near vegetable beds
Spraying every insect immediately without identification
Removing all flowering plants
Burning all garden borders
questions.correctAnswer: Planting flowering herbs near vegetable beds
questions.explanation: Flowering plants can attract pollinators and natural enemies of pests.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply biodiversity practices in organic gardening.

questions.prompt: A vegetable bed has yellowing leaves and poor growth. Which investigation is most useful before adding compost?
options: Check soil moisture, drainage, pest signs, and previous crop records
Guess the problem without observing the bed
Remove labels from all crops
Cover the plants with dirty sacks
questions.correctAnswer: Check soil moisture, drainage, pest signs, and previous crop records
questions.explanation: Observation and records help learners identify likely causes before choosing a solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze crop growth problems before selecting organic management practices.

questions.prompt: Which plan best creates a sustainable organic garden for a school term?
options: Prepare compost, rotate crops, mulch beds, conserve water, and keep records
Plant one crop repeatedly without soil care
Use only dirty wastewater and no crop observations
Harvest before planting and ignore pests
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare compost, rotate crops, mulch beds, conserve water, and keep records
questions.explanation: A sustainable plan combines soil fertility, crop diversity, water management, pest care, and monitoring.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple organic gardening plan for sustained food production.

questions.prompt: What is the main aim of storing crop produce properly?
options: To maintain quality and reduce post-harvest losses
To make produce spoil faster
To remove all food from the community
To mix clean produce with waste
questions.correctAnswer: To maintain quality and reduce post-harvest losses
questions.explanation: Good storage protects produce from moisture, pests, contamination, and spoilage.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of proper crop produce storage.

questions.prompt: Which condition is most important before storing cereals or pulses?
options: They should be dried to a safe moisture level
They should be soaked in dirty water
They should be stored with fresh leaves
They should be mixed with stones
questions.correctAnswer: They should be dried to a safe moisture level
questions.explanation: Dry produce is less likely to develop mould, heat, or pest problems during storage.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify drying as a key preparation step before crop storage.

questions.prompt: Which storage practice helps prevent rodents from damaging crop produce?
options: Seal cracks and keep the store clean
Scatter grain on the floor
Leave doors open at night
Keep food near rubbish heaps
questions.correctAnswer: Seal cracks and keep the store clean
questions.explanation: Clean stores with sealed entry points reduce hiding places and access for rodents.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify practices that reduce pest damage in crop stores.

questions.prompt: Why should crop produce be sorted before storage?
options: To remove damaged, diseased, or infested produce
To make all grains the same colour
To hide spoiled produce in good produce
To increase the amount of dust
questions.correctAnswer: To remove damaged, diseased, or infested produce
questions.explanation: Sorting prevents bad produce from spreading pests or spoilage to good produce.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why sorting is important before storing crop produce.

questions.prompt: Which action improves ventilation in a crop storage room?
options: Arrange bags with spaces for air movement
Block all openings with wet sacks
Pour water between stored bags
Pile bags tightly against every wall
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange bags with spaces for air movement
questions.explanation: Air movement helps reduce heat and moisture buildup in the store.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how ventilation supports safe storage of crop produce.

questions.prompt: Why should sacks of grain be raised on pallets?
options: To reduce contact with floor moisture and allow inspection
To make the grain heavier
To invite termites into the store
To stop learners from counting bags
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce contact with floor moisture and allow inspection
questions.explanation: Pallets keep bags off damp floors and make cleaning and checking easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safe arrangement of crop produce in storage structures.

questions.prompt: A store has a leaking roof above bags of beans. What should learners do first under supervision?
options: Move the beans to a dry place and repair the leak
Open the bags so rain enters faster
Mix wet beans with dry beans
Ignore the leak until all beans sprout
questions.correctAnswer: Move the beans to a dry place and repair the leak
questions.explanation: Protecting the produce from moisture and fixing the source of water prevents spoilage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply corrective actions when storage structures threaten produce quality.

questions.prompt: Which record is most useful when managing stored crop produce?
options: Produce type, date stored, quantity, condition, and pest checks
Only the colour of the sacks
Names of unrelated visitors
The number of windows in the classroom
questions.correctAnswer: Produce type, date stored, quantity, condition, and pest checks
questions.explanation: Storage records help track quality, stock levels, and problems that need action.
questions.learningOutcome: Keep simple records for managing stored crop produce.

questions.prompt: Which sign suggests stored maize may have a pest infestation?
options: Holes in grains and powdery dust
Dry clean grain in labelled bags
Good ventilation in the room
Bags raised on pallets
questions.correctAnswer: Holes in grains and powdery dust
questions.explanation: Holes, dust, insects, or droppings can indicate storage pest activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify signs of pest damage in stored crop produce.

questions.prompt: Why should spoilt produce be removed from a store quickly?
options: It can spread mould, pests, or bad smell to good produce
It improves all produce by contact
It makes storage records unnecessary
It blocks all rodents from entering
questions.correctAnswer: It can spread mould, pests, or bad smell to good produce
questions.explanation: Spoilt produce can contaminate or damage healthy produce if left in storage.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why damaged or spoilt crop produce should be managed promptly.

questions.prompt: A grain store has damp walls, poor air flow, and rodent droppings. Which problem should learners identify?
options: High risk of spoilage and pest damage
Perfect storage conditions
Too much record keeping
A need to add water to the grain
questions.correctAnswer: High risk of spoilage and pest damage
questions.explanation: Moisture, poor ventilation, and rodents are major risks to stored produce.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze storage conditions that can cause post-harvest losses.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares a store before receiving dry beans from a school garden?
options: Clean the store, seal cracks, repair leaks, arrange pallets, and prepare records
Pile beans on a wet floor and close all vents
Mix beans with old spoilt grain
Store beans near an open rubbish pit
questions.correctAnswer: Clean the store, seal cracks, repair leaks, arrange pallets, and prepare records
questions.explanation: A good preparation plan controls moisture, pests, hygiene, arrangement, and monitoring.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe preparation plan for managing stored crop produce.

questions.prompt: In food production, what is a flour mixture?
options: A prepared combination of flour with other ingredients for cooking
A pile of soil mixed with stones
A pesticide solution for crops
A bundle of dry grass for livestock
questions.correctAnswer: A prepared combination of flour with other ingredients for cooking
questions.explanation: Flour mixtures are used to prepare foods such as pancakes, chapati, porridge, or baked products.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify flour mixtures used in food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which ingredient is normally the main dry ingredient in a flour mixture?
options: Flour
Engine oil
Sand
Pesticide powder
questions.correctAnswer: Flour
questions.explanation: Flour is the base ingredient in flour mixtures, while other ingredients adjust texture, taste, or nutrition.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common ingredients in flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: Why should hands and utensils be clean before preparing flour mixtures?
options: To prevent contamination of food
To make flour darker
To stop heat from cooking food
To increase food waste
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent contamination of food
questions.explanation: Clean handling protects food from germs, dirt, and other contaminants.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe hygiene when preparing flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: What is one reason for mixing different flours, such as millet and wheat flour?
options: To improve flavour, texture, or nutrient variety
To make the food unsafe
To replace all cooking heat
To stop the mixture from being edible
questions.correctAnswer: To improve flavour, texture, or nutrient variety
questions.explanation: Composite flour mixtures can improve taste, texture, and nutritional diversity when prepared well.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for using flour mixtures in food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps produce a smooth batter from a flour mixture?
options: Add liquid gradually while stirring
Pour in all liquid and never stir
Mix flour with dry soil
Cook before adding any liquid
questions.correctAnswer: Add liquid gradually while stirring
questions.explanation: Gradual mixing helps prevent lumps and gives a more even batter.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe correct mixing techniques when preparing flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: A learner is preparing a flour mixture for pancakes. Which measurement habit is best?
options: Use the planned recipe quantities accurately
Guess every ingredient without checking
Use any dirty container as a measure
Add salt until the mixture is spoiled
questions.correctAnswer: Use the planned recipe quantities accurately
questions.explanation: Accurate measurement improves texture, taste, cost control, and repeatable results.
questions.learningOutcome: Use accurate measurements when preparing flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which action shows safe cooking of a flour mixture?
options: Cook it thoroughly using clean equipment
Serve it while partly raw and dirty
Place it on a dusty surface after cooking
Use a pan that contains chemical residue
questions.correctAnswer: Cook it thoroughly using clean equipment
questions.explanation: Thorough cooking and clean equipment help make food safe and acceptable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe cooking procedures when using flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: A porridge mixture becomes too thick during cooking. Which adjustment is best?
options: Add clean hot water gradually while stirring
Add sand to make it heavier
Stop stirring and let it burn
Pour in dirty water from the floor
questions.correctAnswer: Add clean hot water gradually while stirring
questions.explanation: Adding clean liquid gradually while stirring adjusts consistency without compromising hygiene.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve simple problems when cooking flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which observation suggests a fried flour mixture product is poorly cooked inside?
options: The outside is brown but the centre is sticky and raw
The product is evenly cooked and firm
The utensils are clean
The ingredients were measured
questions.correctAnswer: The outside is brown but the centre is sticky and raw
questions.explanation: Food can brown outside before the centre cooks if heat is too high or pieces are too thick.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze quality problems in cooked flour mixture products.

questions.prompt: Which plan best reduces waste when preparing flour mixtures for a class practical?
options: Plan portions, measure ingredients, share roles, and store safe leftovers
Cook without a recipe and discard all food
Use more ingredients than needed
Prepare food before washing the work area
questions.correctAnswer: Plan portions, measure ingredients, share roles, and store safe leftovers
questions.explanation: Planning quantities, roles, and storage reduces waste and improves food safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze preparation plans that reduce waste and improve safety.

questions.prompt: Which product plan best shows creativity with locally available flour mixtures?
options: Design a clean recipe combining sorghum flour, wheat flour, safe liquid, and clear cooking steps
Mix unknown powders and serve without cooking
Use dirty water to save time
Ignore taste, hygiene, cost, and nutrition
questions.correctAnswer: Design a clean recipe combining sorghum flour, wheat flour, safe liquid, and clear cooking steps
questions.explanation: A strong plan uses local ingredients, safe handling, clear measurements, and suitable cooking methods.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe food product plan using flour mixtures.

questions.prompt: Why should waste disposal facilities be kept clean in a school agriculture area?
options: To reduce pests, bad smell, and disease risk
To attract flies to food preparation areas
To make compost impossible
To hide sharp waste in paths
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce pests, bad smell, and disease risk
questions.explanation: Clean waste areas protect health and keep the learning environment safe.
questions.learningOutcome: State the importance of cleaning waste disposal facilities.

questions.prompt: Which waste belongs in a compost pit for a school garden?
options: Vegetable peelings
Broken glass
Used batteries
Plastic pen caps
questions.correctAnswer: Vegetable peelings
questions.explanation: Vegetable peelings are biodegradable and can become compost under proper management.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify biodegradable waste for composting.

questions.prompt: Which item should learners wear when cleaning a waste disposal area?
options: Protective gloves
Open food on a plate
A wet paper bag
A dirty cooking spoon
questions.correctAnswer: Protective gloves
questions.explanation: Protective gloves reduce contact with germs, sharp objects, and dirt during cleaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify protective items for cleaning waste disposal facilities.

questions.prompt: Why should waste be sorted before disposal?
options: Different waste types need different safe handling methods
Sorting makes all waste edible
Sorting hides dangerous waste
Sorting stops compost from forming
questions.correctAnswer: Different waste types need different safe handling methods
questions.explanation: Biodegradable, recyclable, and hazardous wastes should not all be handled the same way.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the need for sorting waste before disposal.

questions.prompt: Which action helps control flies around a waste disposal facility?
options: Cover bins and remove waste regularly
Leave food waste uncovered
Pour wastewater around the bin
Store waste beside cooking ingredients
questions.correctAnswer: Cover bins and remove waste regularly
questions.explanation: Covered bins and regular removal reduce breeding sites and access to food waste.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe hygiene practices that reduce pests around waste facilities.

questions.prompt: A compost pit is near a water source and produces runoff during rain. What is the best action?
options: Relocate or improve the pit to prevent water contamination
Let runoff enter the water source
Add plastics to absorb the runoff
Cover the water source with waste
questions.correctAnswer: Relocate or improve the pit to prevent water contamination
questions.explanation: Waste facilities should be managed so that runoff does not contaminate water sources.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe siting and maintenance practices for waste disposal facilities.

questions.prompt: Which cleaning schedule is most suitable for a school waste area?
options: Regular assigned duties with inspection and safe waste removal
Cleaning only after pests have multiplied
No schedule because waste decomposes by itself
Waiting until bad smell reaches classrooms
questions.correctAnswer: Regular assigned duties with inspection and safe waste removal
questions.explanation: A schedule creates responsibility and keeps the waste area safe before problems grow.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize routine cleaning of waste disposal facilities.

questions.prompt: Which plan best improves hygiene and resource use in a school garden waste area?
options: Sort waste, compost organics, cover bins, use gloves, clean regularly, and keep records
Mix all waste in one open heap near the kitchen
Burn every waste item daily without supervision
Hide waste in drainage channels
questions.correctAnswer: Sort waste, compost organics, cover bins, use gloves, clean regularly, and keep records
questions.explanation: A strong waste plan protects health, supports composting, reduces pests, and documents responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe waste management plan for an agricultural learning environment.

questions.prompt: What is grafting in plant production?
options: Joining a scion to a rootstock so they grow as one plant
Drying vegetables in a sun dryer
Sorting beans before storage
Mixing flour with water for cooking
questions.correctAnswer: Joining a scion to a rootstock so they grow as one plant
questions.explanation: Grafting joins plant parts so the scion and rootstock unite and continue growing.
questions.learningOutcome: Define grafting as a plant propagation technique.

questions.prompt: In grafting, what is the scion?
options: The shoot piece chosen for desired fruit or growth qualities
The compost pit beside the garden
The storage sack for beans
The liquid used to cook porridge
questions.correctAnswer: The shoot piece chosen for desired fruit or growth qualities
questions.explanation: The scion is the upper plant part selected for qualities such as fruit type or yield.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the scion in plant grafting.

questions.prompt: In grafting, what is the rootstock?
options: The lower plant part that provides roots
The plastic cover of a sun dryer
The dry grain in a store
The leftover food container
questions.correctAnswer: The lower plant part that provides roots
questions.explanation: The rootstock supplies roots and may contribute traits such as vigour or disease tolerance.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the rootstock in plant grafting.

questions.prompt: Why should grafting tools be sharp and clean?
options: To make smooth cuts and reduce disease transfer
To bruise plant tissues heavily
To contaminate the graft union
To remove the need for tying the graft
questions.correctAnswer: To make smooth cuts and reduce disease transfer
questions.explanation: Clean sharp tools improve contact between tissues and reduce infection risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safety and hygiene requirements when grafting plants.

questions.prompt: Which layer should match closely between scion and rootstock for successful grafting?
options: Cambium layer
Plastic layer
Ash layer
Water layer
questions.correctAnswer: Cambium layer
questions.explanation: Cambium contact allows the joined parts to heal and transport water and nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of cambium contact during grafting.

questions.prompt: Why is a graft union tied or wrapped after joining the plant parts?
options: To hold the parts together and reduce drying
To stop all growth from continuing
To let soil enter the cut surface
To turn the scion into compost
questions.correctAnswer: To hold the parts together and reduce drying
questions.explanation: Wrapping keeps close contact at the union and protects the cut surfaces while healing starts.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe after-joining care in plant grafting.

questions.prompt: A grafted seedling is wilting soon after grafting. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Keep it shaded and moist while checking the wrapping
Expose it to strong sun immediately
Remove all leaves and roots
Pour dirty water on the graft union
questions.correctAnswer: Keep it shaded and moist while checking the wrapping
questions.explanation: New grafts need reduced stress, suitable moisture, and secure wrapping while they heal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply aftercare practices for grafted plants.

questions.prompt: Which pair would most likely improve success in grafting fruit seedlings?
options: Compatible plants and clean matching cuts
Unrelated plants and dirty crushed cuts
Dry scion and loose contact
Rotten rootstock and no wrapping
questions.correctAnswer: Compatible plants and clean matching cuts
questions.explanation: Compatibility, clean cuts, good cambium contact, and secure wrapping are key to successful grafting.
questions.learningOutcome: Select conditions that improve grafting success.

questions.prompt: A graft fails because the scion and rootstock dried out before joining. What was the likely problem?
options: Poor handling allowed plant tissues to lose moisture
The crop storage room was too clean
The compost heap had too many leaves
The flour mixture was too smooth
questions.correctAnswer: Poor handling allowed plant tissues to lose moisture
questions.explanation: Fresh plant tissues must be protected from drying so they can unite after grafting.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze reasons for failure in plant grafting.

questions.prompt: Which plan best guides learners through a grafting practical?
options: Select compatible plants, clean tools, align cambium, wrap the union, label, and monitor
Cut random plants, leave wounds open, and forget labels
Store scions in a hot dry place before grafting
Use blunt dirty tools to save time
questions.correctAnswer: Select compatible plants, clean tools, align cambium, wrap the union, label, and monitor
questions.explanation: A complete grafting plan includes plant choice, hygiene, correct joining, protection, identification, and aftercare.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe sequence for carrying out a plant grafting practical.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a homemade sun dryer?
options: To dry food safely using heat from the sun
To store wet hay in darkness
To make crops grow without soil
To attract pests to vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: To dry food safely using heat from the sun
questions.explanation: A sun dryer uses solar heat and airflow to remove moisture from food for preservation.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of using a homemade sun dryer for food preservation.

questions.prompt: Which food is suitable for preservation in a homemade sun dryer after proper preparation?
options: Thinly sliced vegetables
Wet soil clods
Plastic wrappers
Fresh pesticide containers
questions.correctAnswer: Thinly sliced vegetables
questions.explanation: Clean thin vegetable slices dry faster and more evenly than thick or unsuitable materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify foods suitable for drying in a homemade sun dryer.

questions.prompt: Why should vegetable pieces be cut thinly before sun drying?
options: Thin pieces dry faster and more evenly
Thin pieces never need washing
Thin pieces become poisonous to insects
Thin pieces cannot absorb sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: Thin pieces dry faster and more evenly
questions.explanation: Smaller, even pieces lose moisture more uniformly and reduce the chance of spoilage.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain preparation steps for vegetables before sun drying.

questions.prompt: Which feature helps a sun dryer protect food from contamination?
options: A clean raised tray with a cover or mesh
An open dusty floor
A cracked pesticide tin
A leaking drain beside the tray
questions.correctAnswer: A clean raised tray with a cover or mesh
questions.explanation: A raised covered drying surface keeps food away from dust, animals, and many insects while allowing drying.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe hygiene features of a homemade sun dryer.

questions.prompt: Why is ventilation important in a homemade sun dryer?
options: It allows moist air to leave as food dries
It keeps vegetables wet for longer
It blocks all warm air
It replaces the need for clean food handling
questions.correctAnswer: It allows moist air to leave as food dries
questions.explanation: Airflow carries away moisture, helping food dry faster and reducing mould risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of airflow in solar food drying.

questions.prompt: A learner finds dried vegetables are still soft and damp before storage. What should be done?
options: Continue drying until moisture is low enough for safe storage
Seal them immediately in an airtight jar
Mix them with fresh wet vegetables
Store them in a dirty sack
questions.correctAnswer: Continue drying until moisture is low enough for safe storage
questions.explanation: Damp dried food can spoil in storage, so drying should continue until the product is dry enough.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply quality checks before storing sun-dried vegetables.

questions.prompt: Which storage practice is best for fully dried vegetables?
options: Keep them in clean dry labelled containers
Leave them uncovered overnight
Store them beside wet waste
Mix them with dusty raw vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: Keep them in clean dry labelled containers
questions.explanation: Clean dry labelled containers protect dried vegetables from moisture, pests, and confusion during use.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe storage practices for sun-dried vegetables.

questions.prompt: A sun dryer dries vegetables slowly even on sunny days. Which design change is most useful?
options: Improve airflow and spread pieces in a single layer
Pile vegetables thickly in one corner
Block all vents with cloth
Place wet leaves over the drying tray
questions.correctAnswer: Improve airflow and spread pieces in a single layer
questions.explanation: Better airflow and single-layer arrangement expose more surface area and remove moisture faster.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze sun dryer performance and suggest improvements.

questions.prompt: Which risk should learners manage when using a homemade sun dryer?
options: Contamination from dust, insects, or dirty handling
Vegetables becoming impossible to store if fully dry
Sunlight removing every nutrient completely
Labels causing mould on all containers
questions.correctAnswer: Contamination from dust, insects, or dirty handling
questions.explanation: Food preservation must control contamination as well as moisture loss.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze hygiene risks when preserving vegetables with a sun dryer.

questions.prompt: Which plan best designs a homemade sun dryer for a school vegetable project?
options: Use safe local materials, a raised clean tray, a clear cover, ventilation, labels, and drying records
Dry vegetables on a dusty floor and store them while damp
Build a closed box with no air movement
Use containers that previously held chemicals
questions.correctAnswer: Use safe local materials, a raised clean tray, a clear cover, ventilation, labels, and drying records
questions.explanation: A good sun dryer design combines safe materials, hygiene, heat, airflow, monitoring, and proper records.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe homemade sun dryer plan for preserving vegetables.
